b: Almost always squamous cell carcinoma (about 95%) . It is rare in circumcised men (neonatal circumcision protects) and common where hygiene and circumcision rates are low and HIV and HPV prevalence is high.

Risk factors: lack of circumcision , phimosis and poor hygiene (smegma, chronic balanoposthitis), HPV (types 16 and 18) , multiple sexual partners and STIs, smoking , lichen sclerosus , HIV infection , UV phototherapy for psoriasis.
